A Conditional Construction of Restricted Isometries
abstract: We study the restricted isometry property of a matrix that is built from the discrete Fourier transform matrix by collecting rows indexed by quadratic residues. We find an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \gt 0$</tex> such that, conditioned on a folklore conjecture in number theory, this matrix satisfies the restricted isometry property with sparsity parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K = \Omega ({M^{1/2 + }})$</tex>, where M is the number of rows.

articleTitle: On the sharpness of a three circles theorem for discrete harmonic functions
abstract: In this article we find the sharp error term in an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ}^2$</tex>-three circles theorem for discrete harmonic functions on $\BB{Z}^2$. The proof is highly indirect due to combinatorial obstacles and cancellations phenomena. We exploit Newton interpolation methods and recursive arguments.

articleTitle: Smooth Models of Motivic Spheres and the Clutching Construction
abstract: Abstract We study the representability of motivic spheres by smooth varieties. We show that certain explicit “split” quadric hypersurfaces have the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBA}^1$</tex>-homotopy type of motivic spheres over the integers and that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBA}^1$</tex>-homotopy types of other motivic spheres do not contain smooth schemes as representatives. We then study some applications of these representability/non-representability results to the construction of new exotic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBA}^1$</tex>-contractible smooth schemes. Then, we study vector bundles on even dimensional “split” quadric hypersurfaces by developing an algebro-geometric variant of the classical construction of vector bundles on spheres via clutching functions.

articleTitle: Explicit Characterization of Some Commuting Differential Operators of Rank 2
abstract: Abstract In this article we consider differential operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>. We find the commutativity condition for the operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> with a differential operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> of order 4g + 2, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}/{\BBZ}$</tex> are operators of rank 2. Some examples are constructed. These examples do not commute with differential operators of odd order.

articleTitle: Random and Free Positive Maps with Applications to Entanglement Detection
abstract: We apply random matrix and free probability techniques to the study of linear maps of interest in quantum information theory. Random quantum channels have already been widely investigated with spectacular success. Here, we are interested in more general maps, asking only for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-positivity instead of the complete positivity required of quantum channels. Unlike the theory of completely positive maps, the theory of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-positive maps is far from being completely understood, and our techniques give many new parametrized families of such maps. We also establish a conceptual link with free probability theory and show that our constructions can be obtained to some extent without random techniques in the setup of free products of von Neumann algebras. Finally, we study the properties of our examples and show that for some parameters, they are indecomposable. In particular, they can be used to detect the presence of entanglement missed by the partial transposition test, that is, positive partial transposition entanglement. As an application, we considerably refine our understanding of positive partial transposition states in the case where one of the spaces is large, whereas the other one remains small.

articleTitle: Spectral Types of Linear $q$-Difference Equations and $q$-Analog of Middle Convolution
abstract: We present a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-analog of the middle convolution for linear <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-difference equations with rational coefficients. In the differential case, the middle convolution was defined by Katz, who examined its properties in detail. In this paper, we define a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-analog of the middle convolution. Moreover, we show that it can also be expressed as a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-analog of the Euler transformation. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-middle convolution transforms a Fuchsian equation to a Fuchsian equation and preserves the rigidity index of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>-difference equations.

articleTitle: Speed Exponents of Random Walks on Groups
abstract: Abstract For every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3/4\le \beta \lt 1$</tex> we construct a finitely generated group so that the expected distance of the simple random walk from its starting point satisfies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf E} |X_n|\asymp n^{\beta}$</tex>. In fact, the speed can be set precisely to equal any nice prescribed function up to a constant factor.

articleTitle: Remarks on the Fractional Laplacian with Dirichlet Boundary Conditions and Applications
abstract: Abstract We prove nonlinear lower bounds and commutator estimates for the Dirichlet fractional Laplacian in bounded domains. The applications include bounds for linear drift-diffusion equations with nonlocal dissipation and global existence of weak solutions of critical surface quasi-geostrophic equations.

articleTitle: There Are Infinitely Many Rational Diophantine Sextuples
abstract: A rational Diophantine m-tuple is a set of m non zero rationals such that the product of any two of them increased by 1 is a perfect square. The first rational Diophantine quadruple was found by Diophantus, while Euler proved that there are infinitely many rational Diophantine quintuples. In 1999, Gibbs found the first example of a rational Diophantine sextuple. In this paper, we prove that there exist infinitely many rational Diophantine sextuples.

articleTitle: On Lower Volume Growth Estimate for $({M^m},\bar g,f)$-Minimal Submanifolds in Gradient Shrinking Soliton
abstract: Abstract Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> be a complete gradient shrinking soliton with convex potential <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>. We show that any complete noncompact properly immersed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\Sigma ^n}$</tex>-minimal submanifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${M^m}$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> must have at least linear volume growth. This is a Calabi–Yau type volume growth estimate.

articleTitle: Non-Archimedean Whittaker Functions as Characters: A Probabilistic Approach to the Shintani–Casselman–Shalika Formula
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> be reductive group over a non-Archimedean local field (e.g., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_n( {\BBQ}_p )$</tex> ) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G^\vee( {\BBC} )$</tex> its Langlands dual. Jacquet’s Whittaker function on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is essentially proportional to the character of an irreducible representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G^\vee( {\BBC} )$</tex> (a Schur function if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G = GL_n( {\BBQ}_p )$</tex>). We propose a probabilistic approach to this claim, known as the Shintani–Casselman–Shalika formula, when the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> has at least one minuscule cocharacter. Thanks to random walks on the group, we start by establishing a Poisson kernel formula for the non-Archimedean Whittaker function. The expression and its ingredients are similar to the one previously obtained by the author in the Archimedean case, hence a unified point of view.

articleTitle: Independence of the Zeros of Elliptic Curve $L$-Functions over Function Fields
abstract: Abstract The linear independence (LI) hypothesis, which states roughly that the imaginary parts of the critical zeros of Dirichlet <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions are linearly independent over the rationals, is known to have interesting consequences in the study of prime number races, as pointed out by Rubinstein and Sarnak. In this article, we prove that a function field analog of LI holds generically within certain families of elliptic curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions and their symmetric powers. More precisely, for certain algebro-geometric families of elliptic curves defined over the function field of a fixed curve over a finite field, we give strong quantitative bounds for the number of elements in the family for which the relevant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>-functions have their zeros as linearly independent over the rationals as possible.

articleTitle: Complex Semigroups for Oscillator Groups
abstract: Abstract An oscillator group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is a semidirect product of a Heisenberg group with a one-parameter group. In this article, we construct Olshanski semigroups for infinite-dimensional oscillator groups. These are complex involutive semigroups which have a polar decomposition. The main application will be for representations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> which are semibounded, that is, there exists a non-empty open subset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex> of the Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Fraktur{g}$</tex> such that the operators <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i\rm { d}\pi(x)$</tex> from the derived representation are uniformly bounded from above for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x\in U$</tex>. More precisely, we show that every semibounded representation of an oscillator group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> extends to a non-degenerate holomorphic representation of such a semigroup and conversely each non-degenerate holomorphic representation of such a semigroup gives rise to a semibounded representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>. An important application of this result is a classification of representations of the canonical commutation relations with a positive Hamiltonian, which will be obtained in a subsequent paper. Moreover it yields direct integral decomposition into irreducible ones and implies the existence of a dense subspace of analytic vectors for semibounded representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>.

articleTitle: Global Jacquet-Langlands Correspondence for Division Algebras in Characteristic $p$
abstract: We prove a full global Jacquet–Langlands correspondence between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL(n)$</tex> and division algebras over global fields of non-zero characteristic. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> is a central division algebra of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n^{2}$</tex> over a global field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> of non-zero characteristic, we prove that there exists an injective map from the set of automorphic representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D^{\times}$</tex> to the set of automorphic square integrable representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_n(F)$</tex>, compatible at all places with the local Jacquet–Langlands correspondence for unitary representations. We characterize the image of the map. As a consequence we get multiplicity one and strong multiplicity one theorems for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D^{\times}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Edge Disjoint Hamiltonian Cycles in Highly Connected Tournaments
abstract: Thomassen conjectured that there is a function f(k) such that every strongly f(k)-connected tournament contains k edge-disjoint Hamiltonian cycles. This conjecture was recently proved by Kühn, Lapinskas, Osthus, and Patel who showed that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f(k) \le O({k^2}{(\log k)^2})$</tex> and conjectured that there is a constant C such that f(k) ≤ Ck<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. We prove this conjecture. As a second application of our methods, we answer a question of Thomassen about spanning linkages in highly connected tournaments.

articleTitle: A Transference Approach to a Roth-Type Theorem in the Squares
abstract: Abstract We show that any subset of the squares of positive relative upper density contains nontrivial solutions to a translation-invariant linear equation in five or more variables, with explicit quantitative bounds. As a consequence, we establish the partition regularity of any diagonal quadric in five or more variables whose coefficients sum to zero. Unlike previous approaches, which are limited to equations in seven or more variables, we employ transference technology of Green to import bounds from the linear setting.

articleTitle: Circle Complexes and the Discrete CKP Equation
abstract: In the spirit of Klein's Erlangen Program, we investigate the geometric and algebraic structure of fundamental line complexes and the underlying privileged discrete integrable system for the minors of a matrix which constitute associated Plücker coordinates. Particular emphasis is put on the restriction to Lie circle geometry which is intimately related to the master discrete CKP equation of discrete integrable systems theory. The geometric interpretation, construction, and integrability of fundamental line complexes in Möbius, Laguerre, and hyperbolic geometry are discussed in detail. In the process, we encounter various avatars of classical and novel incidence theorems and associated cross- and multi-ratio identities for particular hypercomplex numbers. This leads to a discrete integrable equation which, in the context of Möbius geometry, governs novel doubly hexagonal circle patterns.

articleTitle: Computations in Symmetric Fusion Categories in Characteristic p
abstract: We study properties of symmetric fusion categories in characteristic p. In particular, we introduce the notion of a super Frobenius–Perron dimension of an object X of such a category and derive an explicit formula for the Verlinde fiber functor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F(X)$</tex> of X (defined by the 2nd author) in terms of the usual and super Frobenius–Perron dimensions of X. We also compute the decomposition of symmetric powers of objects of the Verlinde category, generalizing a classical formula of Cayley and Sylvester for invariants of binary forms. Finally, we show that the Verlinde fiber functor is unique and classify braided fusion categories of rank 2 and triangular semisimple Hopf algebras in any characteristic.

articleTitle: Rank n Swapping Algebra for the PSL(n, ${\BBR}$) Hitchin Component
abstract: Labourie [19] characterized the Hitchin components for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm{PSL}}(n,) {\BBR}$</tex> for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \gt 1$</tex> by using swapping algebra, where the swapping algebra is understood as a ring equipped with a Poisson bracket. We introduce rank n swapping algebra, which is the quotient of the swapping algebra by the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n + 1) \times (n + 1)$</tex> determinant relations. The main results are the well-definedness of the rank n swapping algebra and the “cross-ratio” in its fraction algebra. As a consequence, we use the sub-fraction algebra of the rank n swapping algebra generated by these “cross-ratios” to characterize the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm{PSL}}(n,) {\BBR}$</tex> Hitchin component for a fixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \gt 1$</tex>. We also show the relation between the rank 2 swapping algebra and the cluster <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal X}_{{\rm{PGL}}(2,),{\BBR}{D_k}}}$</tex>-space.

articleTitle: Zeros of Random Functions Generated with de Branges Kernels
abstract: Abstract We study the point process given by the set of real zeros of random series generated with orthonormal bases of reproducing kernels of de Branges spaces. We find an explicit formula for the intensity function in terms of the phase of the Hermite–Biehler function generating the de Branges space. We prove that the intensity of the point process completely characterizes the underlying de Branges space.

articleTitle: Finite Dimensional Hopf Actions on Central Division Algebras
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBK}$</tex> be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> be a division algebra of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> over its center <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z(D)$</tex>. Assume that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \subset Z(D)$</tex>. We show that a finite group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> faithfully grades <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> contains a normal abelian subgroup of index dividing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>. We also prove that if a finite dimensional Hopf algebra coacts on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> defining a Hopf–Galois extension, then its PI degree is at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${d^2}$</tex>. Finally, we construct Hopf–Galois actions on division algebras of twisted group algebras attached to bijective cocycles.

articleTitle: Exponentially Twisted Cyclic Homology
abstract: By a theorem of Bernhard Keller, the de Rham cohomology of a smooth variety is isomorphic to the periodic cyclic homology of the differential graded category of perfect complexes on the variety. Both the de Rham cohomology and the cyclic homology can be twisted by the exponential of a regular function on the variety. We explain that the isomorphism holds true in the twisted setting and draw some conclusions on derived invariance of the algebraic Gauss–Manin systems associated with regular functions.

articleTitle: S1-Equivariant Symplectic Homology and Linearized Contact Homology
abstract: Abstract We present three equivalent definitions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${S^1}$</tex>-equivariant symplectic homology. We show that, using rational coefficients, the positive part of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${S^1}$</tex>-equivariant symplectic homology is isomorphic to linearized contact homology when the latter is defined. We present several computations and applications, and introduce a substitute for cylindrical/linearized contact homology based on an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal S} = \mathop \cup \limits_{n \ge 1} {{\cal S}_n}$</tex>-equivariant construction.

articleTitle: On Gauss Maps in Positive Characteristic in View of Images, Fibers, and Field Extensions
abstract: Abstract The Gauss map of a projective variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X \subset {\BBP}^N$</tex> is a rational map from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> to a Grassmann variety. In positive characteristic, we show the following results. (1) For given projective varieties <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>, we construct a projective variety <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> whose Gauss map has <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> as its general fiber and has <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> as its image. More generally, we give such construction for families of varieties over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex> instead of fixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>. (2) At least in the case when the characteristic is not equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>, any inseparable field extension appears as the extension induced from the Gauss map of some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>.

articleTitle: Lower Bounds for Uncentered Maximal Functions in Any Dimension
On Regularised Quantum Dimensions of the Singlet Vertex Operator Algebra and False Theta Functions
abstract: We study a family of non-C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-cofinite vertex operator algebras, called the singlet vertex operator algebras, and connect several important concepts in the theory of vertex operator algebras, quantum modular forms, and modular tensor categories. More precisely, starting from explicit formulae for characters of modules over the singlet vertex operator algebra, which can be expressed in terms of false theta functions and their derivatives, we first deform these characters by using a complex parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex>. We then apply modular transformation properties of regularisedpartial theta functions to study asymptotic behaviour of regularised characters of irreducible modules and compute their regularised quantum dimensions. We also give a purely geometric description of the regularisation parameter as a uniformisation parameter of the fusion variety coming from atypical blocks. It turns out that the quantum dimensions behave very differently depending on the sign of the real part of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex>. The map from the space of characters equipped with the Verlinde product to the space of regularised quantum dimensions turns out to be a genuine ring isomorphism for positive real part of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex>, while for sufficiently negative real part of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBR}}^d$</tex> its surjective image gives the fusion ring of a rational vertex operator algebra. The category of modules of this rational vertex operator algebra should be viewed as obtained through the process of a semi-simplification procedure widely used in the theory of quantum groups. Interestingly, the modular tensor category structure constants of this vertex operator algebra can be also detected from vector-valued quantum modular forms formed by distinguished atypical characters.

articleTitle: Hodge Type Theorems for Arithmetic Manifolds Associated to Orthogonal Groups
abstract: Abstract We show that special cycles generate a large part of the cohomology of locally symmetric spaces associated to orthogonal groups. We prove in particular that classes of totally geodesic submanifolds generate the cohomology groups of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> of compact congruence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-dimensional hyperbolic manifolds “of simple type” as long as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is strictly smaller than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{p}{3}$</tex>. We also prove that for connected Shimura varieties associated to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O} (p,2)$</tex> the Hodge conjecture is true for classes of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< \frac{p+1}{3}$</tex>. The proof of our general theorem makes use of the recent endoscopic classification of automorphic representations of orthogonal groups by [6]. As such our results are conditional on the hypothesis made in this article, whose proofs have only appeared in preprint form so far; see the second paragraph of Section 1.3.1 below.

articleTitle: The Decoration Theorem for Mandelbrot and Multibrot Sets
abstract: Abstract We prove the decoration theorem for the Mandelbrot set (and Multibrot sets) which says that when a “little Mandelbrot set” is removed from the Mandelbrot set, then most of the resulting connected components have small diameters. By universality of the Mandelbrot set similar results hold for quadratic-like families.

articleTitle: Silting Modules over Commutative Rings
abstract: Abstract Tilting modules over commutative rings were recently classified in [13]: they correspond bijectively to faithful Gabriel topologies of finite type. In this note we extend this classification by dropping faithfulness. The counterpart of an arbitrary Gabriel topology of finite type is obtained by replacing tilting with the more general notion of a silting module.

articleTitle: Linear Stability of the Skyrmion
abstract: Abstract We give a rigorous proof for the linear stability of the Skyrmion. In addition, we provide new proofs for the existence of the Skyrmion and the GGMT bound.

articleTitle: On the Heat Diffusion for Generic Riemannian and Sub-Riemannian Structures
The Rigorous Derivation of the 2D Cubic Focusing NLS from Quantum Many-Body Evolution
abstract: Abstract We consider a 2D time-dependent quantum system of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-bosons with harmonic external confining and attractive interparticle interaction in the Gross–Pitaevskii scaling. We derive stability of matter type estimates proving that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>th power of the energy controls the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^{1}$</tex> Sobolev norm of the solution over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> particles. This estimate is new and more difficult for attractive interactions than repulsive interactions. For the proof, we use a version of the finite-dimensional quantum de Finetti theorem from [47]. A high particle-number averaging effect is at play in the proof, which is not needed for the corresponding estimate in the repulsive case. This a priori bound allows us to prove that the corresponding BBGKY hierarchy converges to the GP limit as was done in many previous works treating the case of repulsive interactions. As a result, we obtain that the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation is the mean-field limit of the 2D time-dependent quantum many-body system with attractive interatomic interaction and asymptotically factorized initial data. An assumption on the size of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{1}$</tex>-norm of the interatomic interaction potential is needed that corresponds to the sharp constant in the 2D Gagliardo–Nirenberg inequality though the inequality is not directly relevant because we are dealing with a trace instead of a power.

articleTitle: Embeddedness of Spheres in Homogeneous Three-Manifolds
abstract: Abstract Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> denote a metric Lie group diffeomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^3$</tex> that admits an algebraic open book decomposition. In this article we prove that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma$</tex> is an immersed surface in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> whose left invariant Gauss map is a diffeomorphism onto <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\S^2$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma$</tex> is an embedded sphere. As a consequence, we deduce that any constant mean curvature sphere of index one in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is embedded.

articleTitle: Euler Characteristics of Hilbert Schemes of Points On Surfaces with Simple Singularities
Correction to “On Satake parameters for representations with parahoric fixed vectors”
abstract: Abstract The main purpose of this note is to correct the statement of [5, Lemma 8.2]. The source of the mistake was an erroneous result in a previous article, namely [4, Lemma 11.12.3]. This note proves corrected versions of both lemmas, and provides counterexamples to the original statements.

articleTitle: Counterexample to the Generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker Inequality for Threefolds
abstract: Abstract We give a counterexample to the generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker inequality for threefolds conjectured by Bayer, Macrì, and Toda using the blow up of a point in three-dimensional projective space.

articleTitle: On Nica-Pimsner Algebras of C*-Dynamical Systems Over ${\BBZ}_+^n$
abstract: We examine Nica-Pimsner algebras associated with semigroup actions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ}_+^n$</tex> on a C*-algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$*$</tex>-endomorphisms. We give necessary and sufficient conditions on the dynamics for exactness and nuclearity of the Nica-Pimsner algebras. Furthermore, we parameterize the KMS states at finite temperature by the tracial states on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>. A parametrization is also shown for KMS states at zero temperature (resp. ground states) by the tracial states on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> (resp. states on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>). Finally, we give a formula for obtaining tracial states on the Nica-Pimsner algebras.

articleTitle: Variants of Geometric RSK, Geometric PNG, and the Multipoint Distribution of the Log-Gamma Polymer
abstract: Abstract We show that the reformulation of the geometric Robinson–Schensted–Knuth correspondence via local moves, introduced in [29], can be extended to cases where the input matrix is replaced by more general polygonal, Young-diagram-like, arrays of the form. We also show that a rearrangement of the sequence of the local moves gives rise to a geometric version of the polynuclear growth model. These reformulations are used to obtain integral formulae for the Laplace transform of the joint distribution of the point-to-point partition functions of the log-gamma polymer at different space–time points. In the case of two points at equal time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> and space at distance of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N^{2/3}$</tex>, we show formally that the joint law of the partition functions, scaled by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N^{1/3}$</tex>, converges to the two-point function of the Airy process.

articleTitle: Sarason Conjecture on the Bergman Space
Diophantine Approximation on Manifolds and the Distribution of Rational Points: Contributions to the Convergence Theory
abstract: In memory of Klaus Roth (October 29, 1925 – November 10, 2015). In this article, we develop the convergence theory of simultaneous, inhomogeneous Diophantine approximation on manifolds. A consequence of our main result is that if the manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal{M} \subset {\BBR}^n$</tex> is of dimension strictly greater than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n+1)/2$</tex> and satisfies a natural non-degeneracy condition, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal{M}$</tex> is of Khintchine type for convergence. The key lies in obtaining essentially the best possible upper bound regarding the distribution of rational points near manifolds.

articleTitle: Characterizing Closed Curves on Riemann Surfaces via Homology Groups of Coverings
On Galois action in rigid DAHA modules
abstract: Given an elliptic curve over a field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> of algebraic numbers, we associate with it an action of the absolute Galois group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_K$</tex> in the type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_1$</tex> rigid DAHA modules at roots of unity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex> and over the rings <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ}[q^{1/4}]/(p^m)$</tex> for sufficiently general prime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>. We describe rigid modules in characteristic zero and for such rings. The main examples of rigid modules are generalized nonsymmetric Verlinde algebras; their deformations for arbitrary <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex> are constructed in this paper, which is of independent interest on its own. The Galois action preserves the images of the elliptic braid group in the groups of automorphisms of rigid modules over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ}[q^{1/4}]/(p^m)$</tex>. If they are finite in characteristic zero, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_K$</tex> acts there and no reduction modulo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(p^m)$</tex> is needed; we find all such cases. In the case of three-dimensional DAHA modules, these images are quotients of equilateral triangle groups directly related to the Livné groups. Also, this paper can be viewed as a certain extension of the DAHA theory of refined Jones polynomials of torus knots (for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_1$</tex>) to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_K$</tex>.

articleTitle: On the Weil–Petersson Curvature of the Moduli Space of Riemann Surfaces of Large Genus
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_g$</tex> be a closed surface of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBM}_g$</tex> be the moduli space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_g$</tex> endowed with the Weil–Petersson metric. In this article we investigate the Weil–Petersson curvatures of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBM}_g$</tex> for large genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>. First, we study the asymptotic behavior of the extremal Weil–Petersson holomorphic sectional curvatures at certain thick surfaces in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBM}_g$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g \to \infty$</tex>. Then we prove two curvature properties on the whole space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBM}_g$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\to \infty$</tex> in a probabilistic way.

articleTitle: A Cohomological Hasse Principle Over Two-dimensional Local Rings
abstract: Abstract Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> be the fraction field of a two-dimensional henselian, excellent, and equi-characteristic local domain. We prove a local–global principle for Galois cohomology with certain finite coefficients over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>. We use classical machinery from étale cohomology theory, drawing upon an idea in Saito’s work on two-dimensional local class field theory. This approach works equally well over the function field of a curve over an equi-characteristic henselian discrete valuation field, thereby giving a different proof of (a slightly generalized version of) a recent result of Harbater, Hartmann, and Krashen. We also present two applications. One is the Hasse principle for torsors under quasi-split semisimple simply connected groups without <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_8$</tex> factor. The other gives an explicit upper bound for the Pythagoras number of a Laurent series field in three variables. This bound is sharper than earlier estimates.

articleTitle: Gal(Qp/Qp) as a geometric fundamental group
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> be a prime number. In this article we present a theorem, suggested by Peter Scholze, which states that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {Gal}(\overline{{\bf Q}}_p/{\bf Q}_p)$</tex> is the étale fundamental group of a certain object <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z$</tex> which is defined over an algebraically closed field. This object is the quotient of the “punctured perfectoid open disk” by an action of the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bf Q}_p^\times$</tex>. !The proof of this fact combines two themes: the tilting equivalence for perfectoid spaces, and the Fargues–Fontaine curve.

articleTitle: Unique Continuation at Infinity for Conical Ricci Expanders
abstract: We establish Carleman inequalities for the weighted Laplacian associated with an expanding gradient Ricci soliton. As a consequence, a unique continuation at infinity is proved for asymptotically Ricci flat Ricci expanders. The obstruction at infinity is a symmetric two-tensor defined on the link of the corresponding asymptotic cone.

articleTitle: Fourier Transforms of C*-Algebras of Nilpotent Lie Groups
abstract: For any nilpotent Lie group G we provide a description of the image of its C*-algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${C^*}(G)$</tex> through its operator-valued Fourier transform. Specifically, we show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${C^*}(G)$</tex> admits a finite composition series such that that the spectra of the corresponding quotients are Hausdorff sets in the relative topology, defined in terms of the fine stratification of the space of coadjoint orbits of G, and the canonical fields of elementary C*-algebras defined by the successive subquotients are trivial. We give a description of the image of the Fourier transform as a C*-algebra of piecewise continuous operator fields on the spectrum, determined by the boundary behavior of the restrictions of operator fields to the spectra of the subquotients in the composition series. For uncountable families of three-step nilpotent Lie groups and also for a sequence of nilpotent Lie groups of arbitrarily high nilpotency step, we prove that every continuous trace subquotient of their C*-algebras has its Dixmier–Douady invariant equal to zero.

articleTitle: Modified Logarithmic Potential Theory and Applications
abstract: We develop potential theory including a Bernstein-Walsh type estimate for functions of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p(g(z))q(f(z))$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p,q$</tex> are polynomials and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f,g$</tex> are holomorphic. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g(z)=z$</tex>, such functions arise in the study of certain ensembles of probability measures and in this case we can further extend the theory leading to probabilistic results such as large deviation principles.

articleTitle: On Pluricanonical Locally Conformally Kähler Manifolds
abstract: Abstract We prove that compact pluricanonical locally conformally Kähler manifolds have parallel Lee form.

articleTitle: Divisorial Strata of Abelian Differentials
abstract: Abstract We compute a closed formula for the class of the closure of the locus of curves in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa = ({k_1}, \ldots ,{k_{g - 2}})$</tex> that admit an abelian differential of signature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal M}_\gamma }$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Lifting of an Automorphism of a K3 Surface over Odd Characteristic
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we prove that, over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic, a weakly tame automorphism of a K3 surface of finite height can be lifted over the ring of Witt vectors of the base field. Also we prove that a non-symplectic tame automorphism of a supersingular K3 surface or a symplectic tame automorphism of a supersingular K3 surface of Artin-invariant at least 2 can be lifted to the ring of Witt vectors. Using these results, we prove, for a weakly tame K3 surface of finite height, there is a lifting over the ring of Witt vectors to which the entire automorphism group extends. Also we prove a K3 surface equipped with a purely non-symplectic automorphism of a certain high order is unique up to isomorphism. The following is the outline of the paper. In Section 1, we review some background of the problem and state the main results. In Section 2, we recall the deformation theory of K3 surfaces defined over a field of positive characteristic and prove that formal liftings of a K3 surface over the Witt vectors are classified by the Hodge structure on the second crystalline cohomology. In Section 3, we prove the main results based on the classification of liftings and some properties of the crystalline cohomology of K3 surfaces. In Section 4, we prove, using the main result, the uniqueness of a tame purely non-symplectic automorphism of some high order of a K3 surface over a field of positive characteristic.

articleTitle: Linear Pencils Encoded in the Newton Polygon
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> be an algebraic curve defined by a sufficiently generic bivariate Laurent polynomial with given Newton polygon <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex>. It is classical that the geometric genus of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> equals the number of lattice points in the interior of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta$</tex>. In this paper we give similar combinatorial interpretations for the gonality, the Clifford index, and the Clifford dimension, by removing a technical assumption from a recent result of Kawaguchi. More generally, the method shows that apart from certain well-understood exceptions, every base-point free pencil whose degree equals or slightly exceeds the gonality is combinatorial, in the sense that it corresponds to projecting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> along a lattice direction. Along the way we prove various features of combinatorial pencils. For instance, we give an interpretation for the scrollar invariants associated with a combinatorial pencil, and show how one can tell whether the pencil is complete or not. A similar interpretation for its first scrollar Betti numbers (as introduced by Schreyer) is also given. Among the applications, we find that every smooth projective curve admits at most one Weierstrass semi-group of embedding dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex>, and that if a non-hyperelliptic smooth projective curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g \geq 2$</tex> can be embedded in the nth Hirzebruch surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal{H}_n$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is actually an invariant of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>. This article comes along with three Magma files: basic_commands.m, gonal.m, neargonal.m

articleTitle: A Discrete Quadratic Carleson Theorem on with ℓ2 a Restricted Supremum
abstract: Consider the discrete maximal function acting on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${{\cal C}_{\rm{\Lambda }}}f(n): = \mathop {\sup }\limits_{\lambda \in {\rm{\Lambda }}} \left| {\mathop \sum \limits_{m \ne 0} f(n - m){{{{\rm{e}}^{2\pi {\rm{i}}\lambda {m^2}}}} \over m},} \right|$$</tex> functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm{\Lambda }} \subset [0,1]$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm{\Lambda }}$</tex>. We give sufficient conditions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${L^2}({\BBR})$</tex>, met by certain kinds of Cantor sets, for this to be a bounded sublinear operator. This result is a discrete analogue of E.M.Stein’s integral result, that the maximal operator below is bounded on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${{\cal C}_2}f(x): = \mathop {\sup }\limits_{\lambda \in } \left| {\smallint f(x - y){{{{\rm{e}}^{2\pi {\rm{i}}\lambda {y^2}}}} \over y}{\rm{d}}y} \right|.$$</tex>. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda $</tex> The proof of our result relies heavily on Bourgain’s work on arithmetic ergodic theorems, with novel complexity arising from the oscillatory nature of the question at hand, and difficulties arising from the parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${S^1}$</tex> above.

articleTitle: Variants of the Busemann–Petty Problem and of the Shephard Problem
Cylinders in del Pezzo Surfaces
abstract: On del Pezzo surfaces, we study effective ample <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}$</tex>-divisors such that the complements of their supports are isomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBA}^1$</tex>-bundles over smooth affine curves. All considered varieties are assumed to be algebraic and defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex> throughout this article.

articleTitle: Erratum to “Automorphisms with Quasi-discrete Spectrum, Multiplicative Functions and Average Orthogonality Along Short Intervals”
Asymptotics of the Weil–Petersson Metric
abstract: Abstract We consider the Riemann moduli space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma \gt 1$</tex> of conformal structures on a compact surface of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${g_{{\rm{WP}}}}$</tex> together with its Weil–Petersson metric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${g_{{\rm{WP}}}}$</tex>. Our main result is that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal M}_\gamma }$</tex> admits a complete polyhomogeneous expansion in powers of the lengths of the short geodesics up to the singular divisors of the Deligne–Mumford compactification of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>.

articleTitle: Shifted Convolution Sums of ${A_f}(1,n)$ Cusp Forms with θ-Series
abstract: Abstract Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> be the normalized Fourier coefficients of a Hecke–Maass cusp form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S{L_3}({\BBZ})$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${r_3}(n) = \# \left\{ {({n_1},{n_2},{n_3}) \in {\BBZ}{^3}:n_1^2 + n_2^2 + n_3^2 = n} \right\}.$$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \le h \le X$</tex> Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi (x)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[1/2,1]$</tex> be a smooth function compactly supported on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon \gt 0$</tex>. It is proved that for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\mathop \sum \limits_{n \ge 1} {A_f}(1,n + h){r_3}(n)\phi \left( {{n \over X}} \right){ \ll _{f,\varepsilon }}{X^{{3 \over 2} - {1 \over 8} + \varepsilon }}$$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> uniformly with respect to the shift <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L = d_x^4 + u(x)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Geodesics of Positive Lagrangians in Milnor Fibers
abstract: The space of positive Lagrangians in an almost Calabi–Yau manifold is an open set in the space of all Lagrangian submanifolds. A Hamiltonian isotopy class of positive Lagrangians admits a natural Riemannian metric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Upsilon $</tex>, which gives rise to a notion of geodesics. We study geodesics of positive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${O_n}({\BBR})$</tex> invariant Lagrangian spheres in n-dimensional A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> Milnor fibers. We show the existence and uniqueness of smooth solutions to the initial value problem and the boundary value problem. In particular, we obtain examples of smooth geodesics of positive Lagrangians in arbitrary dimension. As an application, we show that the Riemannian metric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Upsilon $</tex> induces a metric space structure on the space of positive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${O_n}({\BBR})$</tex> invariant Lagrangian spheres in the above-mentioned Milnor fibers.

articleTitle: The Einstein–Hilbert Functional and the Sasaki–Futaki Invariant
abstract: Abstract We show that the Einstein–Hilbert functional, as a functional on the space of Reeb vector fields, detects the vanishing Sasaki–Futaki invariant. In particular, this provides an obstruction to the existence of a constant scalar curvature Sasakian metric. As an application we prove that K-semistable polarized Sasaki manifold has vanishing Sasaki–Futaki invariant. We then apply this result to show that under the right conditions on the Sasaki join manifolds of [6], a polarized Sasaki manifold admits constant scalar curvature Sasaki metric if it is K-polystable.

articleTitle: On the Loomis-Whitney Inequality for Isotropic Measures
abstract: Abstract The Ball–Loomis–Whitney inequality for isotropic measures is extended from volume to all intrinsic volumes along with a complete description of equality conditions. The proof is based on a reverse intrinsic volume inequality for zonoids.

articleTitle: Supercyclidic Nets
abstract: Supercyclides are surfaces with a characteristic conjugate parameterization consisting of two families of conics. Patches of supercyclides can be adapted to a Q-net (a discrete quadrilateral net with planar faces) such that neighboring surface patches share tangent planes along common boundary curves. We call the resulting patchworks “supercyclidic nets” and show that every Q-net in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}{\rm P}^3$</tex> can be extended to a supercyclidic net. The construction is governed by a multidimensionally consistent three-dimensional system. One essential aspect of the theory is the extension of a given Q-net in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}{\rm P}^N$</tex> to a system of circumscribed discrete torsal line systems. We present a description of the latter in terms of projective reflections that generalizes the systems of orthogonal reflections which govern the extension of circular nets to cyclidic nets by means of Dupin cyclide patches.

articleTitle: Classification of Flexible Kokotsakis Polyhedra with Quadrangular Base
abstract: A Kokotsakis polyhedron with quadrangular base is a neighborhood of a quadrilateral in a quad surface. Generically, a Kokotsakis polyhedron is rigid. In this article we classify flexible Kokotsakis polyhedra with quadrangular bases. The analysis is based on the fact that any pair of adjacent dihedral angles of a Kokotsakis polyhedron is related by a biquadratic equation. This results in a diagram of branched covers of complex projective lines by elliptic curves. A polyhedron is flexible if and only if all repeated fiber products of coverings meet in the same Riemann surface, which is then the configuration space of the polyhedron.

articleTitle: A Family of New-Way Integrals for the Standard ℒ-function of Cuspidal Representations of the Exceptional Group of Type G2
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal{L}^{S}\!\left({s,\pi,\chi, {\Fraktur{st}}}\right)\!$</tex> be a standard twisted partial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal{L}$</tex>-function of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7$</tex> of the cuspidal automorphic representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> of the exceptional group of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_2$</tex>. In this paper, we consider a family of Rankin–Selberg integrals and prove that it represents this <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cal{L}$</tex>-function. As an application, we prove that the representations attaining certain prescribed poles are exactly the representations attained by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex>-lift from a group of\break finite type.

articleTitle: The Degree of the Dormant Operatic Locus
abstract: Abstract Hara-naka ya Mono nimo tsukazu Naku hibari     Matsuo Basho[14] Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> be a smooth, projective curve of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\geq 2$</tex> over an algebraically closed field of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \gt 0$</tex>. I provide a conjectural formula for the degree of the scheme of dormant Projective General Linear <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm PGL}(r)$</tex>-opers on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r\geq 2$</tex> (I assume that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> is greater than an explicit constant depending on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g,r$</tex>). For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r=2$</tex>, a dormant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm PGL}(2)$</tex>-oper is a dormant indigenous bundle on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> in the sense of Shinichi Mochuzki (and his work provides a formula only for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g=2,r=2,p\geq 5$</tex>, from a different point of view). In 2014, Yasuhiro Wakabayashi has shown that my conjectural formula holds for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r=2,g\geq 2$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \gt 2g-2$</tex> and more recently he has proved the conjecture in all ranks for generic curves of genus at least two.

articleTitle: Corrigendum: Unirationality of Hurwitz Spaces of Coverings of Degree $\leq 5$
abstract: Abstract We correct Proposition 3.12 and Lemma 3.13 of the paper published in Vol. 2013, No.13, pp.3006–3052. The corrections do not affect the other statements of the paper.

articleTitle: The Double Gromov–Witten Invariants of Hirzebruch Surfaces are Piecewise Polynomial
abstract: We define the double Gromov–Witten invariants of Hirzebruch surfaces in analogy with double Hurwitz numbers, and we prove that they satisfy a piecewise polynomiality property analogous to their one-dimensional counterpart. Furthermore we show that each polynomial piece is either even or odd, and we compute its degree. Our methods combine floor diagrams and Ehrhart theory.

articleTitle: A Family of Graded Decomposition Numbers for Diagrammatic Cherednik Algebras
abstract: Abstract We provide an algorithmic description of a family of graded decomposition numbers for diagrammatic Cherednik algebras in terms of affine Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.

articleTitle: On the Kähler Ricci Flow on Projective Manifolds of General Type
abstract: We consider the Käahler–Ricci flow on a smooth minimal model of general type, we show that if the Ricci curvature is uniformly bounded below along the Käahler–Ricci flow, then the diameter is uniformly bounded. As a corollary we show that under the Ricci curvature lower bound assumption, the Gromov–Hausdorff limit of the flow is homeomorphic to the canonical model. Moreover, we can give a purely analytic proof of a recent result of Tosatti–Zhang [28] that if the canonical line bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_X$</tex> is big and numerically effective, but not ample, then the flow is of Type IIb.

articleTitle: Narrow Arithmetic Progressions in the Primes
abstract: We study arithmetic progressions in primes with common differences as small as possible. Tao and Ziegler showed that, for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \ge 3$</tex> and N large, there exist nontrivial k-term arithmetic progressions in (any positive density subset of) the primes up to N with common difference <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O({(\log N)^{{L_k}}})$</tex>, for an unspecified constant L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>. In this work, we obtain this statement with the precise value <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${L_k} = (k - 1){2^{k - 2}}$</tex>. This is achieved by proving a relative version of Szemerédi's theorem for narrow progressions requiring simpler pseudorandomness hypotheses in the spirit of recent work of Conlon, Fox, and Zhao.

articleTitle: Liftings of Nichols Algebras of Diagonal Type I. Cartan Type A
abstract: Abstract After the classification of the finite-dimensional Nichols algebras of diagonal type [17, 18], the determination of its defining relations [7, 6], and the verification of the generation in degree-s1 conjecture [6], there is still one step missing in the classification of complex finite-dimensional Hopf algebras with abelian group, without restrictions on the order of the latter: the computation of all deformations or liftings. A technique towards solving this question was developed in [5], built on cocycle deformations. In this paper, we elaborate further and present an explicit algorithm to compute liftings. In our main result we classify all liftings of finite-dimensional Nichols algebras of Cartan type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>, over a cosemisimple Hopf algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \gt $</tex>. This extends [2], where it was assumed that the parameter is a root of unity of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>3 and that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${A_2}$</tex> is a commmutative group algebra. When the parameter is a root of unity of order 2 or 3, new phenomena appear: the quantum Serre relations can be deformed; this allows in turn the power root vectors to be deformed to elements in lower terms of the coradical filtration, but not necessarily in the group algebra. These phenomena are already present in the calculation of the liftings in type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> at a parameter of order 2 or 3 over an abelian group [11, 19], done by a different method using a computer program. As a byproduct of our calculations, we present new infinite families of finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebras.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Liouville Problems in a Quarter Plane
abstract: We answer affirmatively the open problem proposed by Cabré and Tan in their paper “Positive solutions of nonlinear problems involving the square root of the Laplacian” ([4]}).

articleTitle: Equisingularity in One-Parameter Families of Generically Reduced Curves
abstract: We explore some equisingularity criteria in one-parameter families of generically reduced curves. We prove the equivalence between Whitney regularity and Zariski’s discriminant criterion. We prove that topological triviality implies smoothness of the normalized surface. Examples are given to show that Witney regularity and equisaturation are not stable under the blow-up of the singular locus nor under the Nash modification.

articleTitle: A Generalization of Ribet's Nondegeneracy Theorem
abstract: A nondegenerate CM Hodge structure is irreducible. For Weight 1, Ribet's Nondegeneracy Theorem informs us that the converse is true for Hodge numbers (p, p), p being an odd prime. We extend this to all odd weight CM Hodge structures.

articleTitle: A Spectral Sequence of the Floer Cohomology of Symplectomorphisms of Trivial Polarization Class
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> be an exact symplectic manifold equal to a symplectization near infinity and having stably trivializable tangent bundle, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi :M \to M$</tex> be an exact symplectomorphism which, near infinity, is equal to either the identity or the symplectization of a contactomorphism <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat \phi $</tex> such that neither <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat \phi $</tex> nor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\hat \phi ^2}$</tex> has fixed points. We give conditions under which Seidel and Smith's localization theorem for Lagrangian Floer cohomology implies the existence of a spectral sequence from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$HF({\phi ^2}) \otimes {_2}((\theta ))$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$HF(\phi ) \otimes {_2}((\theta ))$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Signature of a Splice
abstract: Abstract We study the behavior of the signature of colored links [6, 9] under the splice operation. We extend the construction to colored links in integral homology spheres and show that the signature is almost additive, with a correction term independent of the links. We interpret this correction term as the signature of a generalized Hopf link and give a simple closed formula to compute it.

articleTitle: Salem Sets with No Arithmetic Progressions
abstract: Abstract We construct compact Salem sets in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> of any dimension (including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>), which do not contain any arithmetic progressions of length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>. Moreover, the sets can be taken to be Ahlfors regular if the dimension is less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex>, and the measure witnessing the Fourier decay can be taken to be Frostman in the case of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}$</tex>. This is in sharp contrast to the situation in the discrete setting (where Fourier uniformity is well known to imply existence of progressions) and helps clarify a result of Łaba and Pramanik on pseudo-random subsets of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> which do contain progressions.

articleTitle: Christoffel Transformations for Matrix Orthogonal Polynomials in the Real Line and the non-Abelian 2D Toda Lattice Hierarchy
abstract: Given a matrix polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W(x)$</tex>, matrix bi-orthogonal polynomials with respect to the sesquilinear form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu(x)$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\left\langle{\cdot, \cdot }\right\rangle}_W$</tex> is a matrix of Borel measures supported in some infinite subset of the real line, are considered. Connection formulas between the sequences of matrix bi-orthogonal polynomials with respect to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu(x)$</tex> and matrix polynomials orthogonal with respect to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W(x)$</tex> are presented. In particular, for the case of nonsingular leading coefficients of the perturbation matrix polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W(x)$</tex> we present a generalization of the Christoffel formula constructed in terms of the Jordan chains of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon$</tex>. For perturbations with a singular leading coefficient, several examples by Durán and coworkers are revisited. Finally, we extend these results to the non-Abelian 2D Toda lattice hierarchy.

articleTitle: A simplicial approach to effective divisors in ${\bar M_{0,n}}$
abstract: We study the Cox ring and monoid of effective divisor classes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bar M_{0,n}} \cong {\rm{Bl}}{^{n - 3}}$</tex>, over a ring R. We provide a bijection between elements of the Cox ring, not divisible by any exceptional divisor section, and pure-dimensional singular simplicial complexes on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left\{ {1, \ldots ,n - 1} \right\}$</tex> with weights in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R \setminus \left\{ 0 \right\}$</tex> satisfying a zero-tension condition. This leads to a combinatorial criterion, satisfied by many triangulations of closed manifolds, for a divisor class to be among the minimal generators for the effective monoid. For classes obtained as the strict transform of quadrics, we present a complete classification of minimal generators, generalizing to all n the well-known Keel–Vermeire classes for n = 6. We use this classification to construct new divisors with interesting properties for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \ge 7$</tex>.

articleTitle: Cantor Spectrum for a Class of $C^2$ Quasiperiodic Schrödinger Operators
abstract: Abstract We show that for a class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^2$</tex> quasiperiodic potentials and for any fixed Diophantine frequency, the spectrum of the corresponding Schrödinger operator is a Cantor set. Our approach is of a purely dynamical systems flavor, which depends on a detailed analysis of asymptotic stable and unstable directions. We also apply it to more general quasiperiodic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {SL}(2,\BBR)$</tex> cocycles and obtain that uniformly hyperbolic systems form an open and dense set in some one-parameter family of dynamical systems.

articleTitle: On the rigidity of moduli of curves in arbitrary characteristic
Weight Homology of Motives
abstract: Abstract In the first half of this article, we define a new weight homology functor on Voevodsky’s category of effective motives and investigate some of its properties. In special cases, we recover Gillet–Soulé’s weight homology and Geisser’s Kato-Suslin homology. In the second half, we consider the notions of “co-étale” and “reduced” motives, and use the notions to a prove a theorem comparing motivic homology to étale motivic homology. Due to [19] we do not have to restrict to smooth schemes.

articleTitle: On the Homology Length Spectrum of Surfaces
abstract: Abstract On a surface with a Finsler metric, we investigate the asymptotic growth of the number of closed geodesics of length less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> which minimize length among all geodesic multicurves in the same homology class. An important class of surfaces which are of interest to us are hyperbolic surfaces.

articleTitle: Bounded Negativity, Miyaoka—Sakai Inequality, and Elliptic Curve Configurations
abstract: Abstract Similar to the linear Harbourne constant recently introduced in [2], we study the elliptic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>-constants of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}^{2}$</tex> and of Abelian surfaces. We also study the Harbourne indices of curves on these surfaces. In particular, we show that there are configurations of smooth plane cubic curves whose Harbourne indices are arbitrarily close to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-4$</tex>.
