Consequently, we obtain that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>-constant of any surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is less than or equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-4$</tex>. Related to these problems, we moreover give a new inequality for the number and multiplicities of singularities of elliptic curves arrangements on Abelian surfaces, inequality which has a close similarity to the one of Hirzebruch for lines arrangements on the plane.

articleTitle: Representation Stability for Cohomology of Configuration Spaces in $S_n$
abstract: This paper studies representation stability in the sense of Church and Farb for representations of the symmetric group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> on the cohomology of the configuration space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBR}}^d$</tex> ordered points in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d-1$</tex>. This cohomology is known to vanish outside of dimensions divisible by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_n$</tex>; it is shown here that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i(d-1){\rm st}$</tex>-representation on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=3i$</tex> cohomology stabilizes sharply at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=3i+1$</tex> (resp. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>) when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_n$</tex> is odd (resp. even). The result comes from analyzing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>-representations known to control the cohomology: the Whitney homology of set partition lattices for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> even, and the higher Lie representations for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\geq 4i$</tex> odd. A similar analysis shows that the homology of any rank-selected subposet in the partition lattice stabilizes by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_n$</tex> is the maximum rank selected. Further properties of the Whitney homology and more refined stability statements for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^2$</tex>-isotypic components are also proven, including conjectures of J. Wiltshire-Gordon.

articleTitle: The Congruence Subgroup Property Does Not Imply Invariable Generation
abstract: Abstract It was suggested in [5] that for arithmetic groups Invariable Generation is equivalent to the Congruence Subgroup Property. In this paper, we dismiss this conjecture by proving that certain %arithmetic groups possessing the CSP are not IG. arithmetic groups which possess the later property do not possess the first one.

articleTitle: A Discrete Parametrized Surface Theory in ℝ3
Finding a Low-dimensional Piece of a Set of Integers
abstract: Abstract We show that a finite set of integers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|A+A| \le K |A|$</tex> contains a large piece <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X \subseteq A$</tex> with Freĭman dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(\log K)$</tex>, where large means <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|A|/|X| \ll \exp(O(\log^2 K))$</tex>. This can be thought of as a major quantitative improvement on Freĭman’s dimension lemma; or as a “weak” Freĭman–Ruzsa theorem with almost polynomial bounds. The methods used, centred around an “additive energy increment strategy”, differ from the usual tools in this area and may have further potential. Most of our argument takes place over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_2^n$</tex>, which is itself curious. There is a possibility that the above bounds could be improved, assuming sufficiently strong results in the spirit of the Polynomial Freĭman–Ruzsa Conjecture over finite fields.

articleTitle: Jordan Algebras and Quantum Bessel Processes
abstract: Abstract A family of multidimensional Markov processes is constructed by restricting a semigroup of positive contractions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{C}^\ast(H)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H=W\times {\BBR}$</tex> is a Heisenberg group and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> is a simple complex Jordan algebra, to some commutative sub-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{C}^\ast$</tex>-algebras of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{C}^\ast(H)$</tex>, associated with certain Gelfand pairs. The constructed processes are multidimensional generalizations of Biane’s quantum Bessel process. As a bonus, a construction of the quantum Bessel process related to the space of rectangular complex matrices is presented.

articleTitle: An Algebro-Geometric Realization of the Cohomology Ring of Hilbert Scheme of Points in the Affine Plane
abstract: Abstract We show that the cohomology ring of Hilbert scheme of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-points in the affine plane is isomorphic to the coordinate ring of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBG}_{m}$</tex>-fixed point scheme of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-th symmetric product of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}^{2}$</tex> for a natural <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBG}_{m}$</tex>-action on it. This result can be seen as an analogue of a theorem of DeConcini–Procesi and Tanisaki on a description of the cohomology ring of Springer fiber of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>. We also prove similar results for type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> S3-varieties and smooth hypertoric varieties. These results can be formulated in terms of the symplectic duality of Braden–Licata–Proudfoot–Webster.

articleTitle: The Number of Zeros of $\zeta '(s)$
abstract: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$${N_1}(T) = {T \over {2\pi }}\log {T \over {4\pi e}} + O\left( {{{\log T} \over {\log \log T}}} \right),$$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${N_1}(T)$</tex> is the number of zeros of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\zeta '(s)$</tex> in the region <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 \lt \Im s \le T$</tex>.

articleTitle: Full Escape of Mass for the Diagonal Group
abstract: Abstract Building on the work of Cassels we prove the existence of infinite families of compact orbits of the diagonal group in the space of lattices which accumulate only on the divergent orbit of the standard lattice. As a consequence, we prove the existence of full escape of mass for sequences of such orbits, sharpening known results about possible partial escape of mass. The topological complexity of the visits of these orbits to a given compact set in the space of lattices is analyzed. Along the way we develop new tools to compute regulators of orders in a number fields.

articleTitle: A Uniform Model for Kirillov–Reshetikhin Crystals II. Alcove Model, Path Model, and $P=X$
abstract: Abstract We establish the equality of the specialization <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_\lambda(x;q,0)$</tex> of the Macdonald polynomial at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t=0$</tex> with the graded character <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_\lambda(x;q)$</tex> of a tensor product of “single-column” Kirillov–Reshetikhin modules for untwisted affine Lie algebras. This is achieved by constructing two uniform combinatorial models for the crystals associated with the mentioned tensor products: the quantum alcove model (which is naturally associated with Macdonald polynomials) and the quantum Lakshmibai–Seshadri path model. We provide an explicit affine crystal isomorphism between the two models, and realize the energy function in both models. In particular, this gives the first proof of the positivity of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t = 0$</tex> limit of the symmetric Macdonald polynomial in the untwisted and non-simply laced cases, when it is expressed as a linear combination of the irreducible characters for a finite-dimensional simple Lie subalgebra, as well as a representation-theoretic meaning of the coefficients in this expression in terms of degree functions.

articleTitle: Dilations, Inclusions of Matrix Convex Sets, and Completely Positive Maps
abstract: Abstract A matrix convex set is a set of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal S}_n}$</tex> (where each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> is a set of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \times n$</tex>-tuples of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${M_n}$</tex> matrices) that is invariant under unital completely positive maps from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${M_k}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal S} = \mathop \cup \limits_{n \ge 1} {{\cal S}_n},$</tex> and under formation of direct sums. We study the geometry of matrix convex sets and their relationship to completely positive maps and dilation theory. Key ingredients in our approach are polar duality in the sense of Effros and Winkler, matrix ranges in the sense of Arveson, and concrete constructions of scaled commuting normal dilation for tuples of self-adjoint operators, in the sense of Helton, Klep, McCullough, and Schweighofer. Given two matrix convex sets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal T} = \mathop \cup \limits_{n \ge 1} {{\cal T}_n}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal S}$</tex>, we find geometric conditions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal T}$</tex> or on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal S}_1} \subseteq {{\cal T}_1}$</tex>, such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal S} \subseteq C{\cal T}$</tex> implies that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> for some constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal S}$</tex>. For instance, under various symmetry conditions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>, we can show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> above can be chosen to equal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C = d$</tex>, the number of variables. We also show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal W}^{\max }}(\overline {{\BBB}{_d}} )$</tex> is sharp for a specific matrix convex set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBB}{_d}$</tex> constructed from the unit ball <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal D}$</tex>. This led us to find an essentially unique self-dual matrix convex set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C = \sqrt d $</tex>, the self-dual matrix ball, for which corresponding inclusion and dilation results hold with constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal T}$</tex>. For a certain class of polytopes, we obtain a considerable sharpening of such inclusion results involving polar duals. An illustrative example is that a sufficient condition for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${^{(d)}} = \mathop \cup \limits_n \left\{ {({T_1}, \ldots ,{T_d}) \in M_n^d:{T_i} \le 1} \right\}$</tex> to contain the free matrix cube <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{ x \in {\BBR}{^d}:\sum |{x_j}| \le 1\} \subseteq {1 \over d}{{\cal T}_1}$</tex>, is that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1 \over d}{{\cal T}_1}$</tex>, that is, that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${[ - 1,1]^d} = _1^{(d)}$</tex> contains the polar dual of the cube <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>. Our results have immediate implications to spectrahedral inclusion problems studied recently by Helton, Klep, McCullough and Schweighofer. Our constants do not depend on the ranks of the pencils determining the free spectrahedra in question, but rather on the “number of variables” <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\matrix{ {{1 \over M}\mathop \sum \limits_{M \le m \lt 2M} {1 \over H}\left| {\mathop \sum \limits_{m \le n \lt m + H} {e^{2\pi iP(n)}}\nu (n)} \right|0} \cr } $$</tex>. There are also implications to the problem of existence of (unital) completely positive maps with prescribed values on a set of operators.

articleTitle: Modular Categories, Crossed S-matrices, and Shintani Descent
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr{C}$</tex> be a modular tensor category over an algebraically closed field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> of characteristic 0. Then there is the ubiquitous notion of the S-matrix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S(\scr{C})$</tex> associated with the modular category. The matrix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S(\scr{C})$</tex> is a symmetric matrix, its entries are cyclotomic integers, and the matrix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\dim \scr{C})^{-{1 \over 2}}\cdot S(\scr{C})$</tex> is a unitary matrix. Here <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dim \scr{C}\in k$</tex> denotes the categorical dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr{C}$</tex> and it is a totally positive cyclotomic integer. Now suppose that we also have a modular autoequivalence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F:\scr{C}\to \scr{C}$</tex>. In this article, we will define and study the notion of a crossed S-matrix associated with the modular autoequivalence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>. We will see that the crossed S-matrix occurs as a submatrix of the usual S-matrix of some “bigger” modular category and hence the entries of a crossed S-matrix are also cyclotomic integers. We will prove that the crossed S-matrix (normalized by the factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\dim \scr{C})^{-{1 \over 2}}$</tex>) associated with any modular autoequivalence is a unitary matrix. We will also prove that the crossed S-matrix is essentially the “character table” of a certain semisimple commutative Frobenius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>-algebra associated with the modular autoequivalence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>. The motivation for most of our results comes from the theory of character sheaves on algebraic groups, where we expect that the transition matrices between irreducible characters and character sheaves can be obtained as certain crossed S-matrices. In the character theory of algebraic groups defined over finite fields, there is the notion of Shintani descent of Frobenius stable characters. We will define and study a categorical analogue of this notion of Shintani descent in the setting of modular categories.

articleTitle: Automorphisms with Quasi-discrete Spectrum, Multiplicative Functions and Average Orthogonality Along Short Intervals
Absence of Eigenvalues for Quasi-Periodic Lattice Operators with Liouville Frequencies
abstract: Dedicated to Barry Simon on the occasion of his 70th birthday We show that a lattice Schrödinger operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta+v$</tex> acting in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBC}^{{\BBZ}^d}$</tex> does not have <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l^2$</tex> eigenfunctions if its potential <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v(\cdot)$</tex> admits fast local approximation by periodic functions. A special case of this result states that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v(x)=V(\alpha_1 x_1,\ldots,\alpha_d x_d)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V(\cdot)$</tex> is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1,\ldots,1)$</tex>-periodic function on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBR}^d$</tex> satisfying the Hölder condition and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d)\in{\BBR}^d$</tex> is a vector admitting fast rational approximation, then the operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta+v$</tex> has no eigenfunctions in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l^2({\BBZ}^d)$</tex>. The one-dimensional case of this statement has been known since 1970s, and the question whether its multidimensional generalization was possible remained open since then.

articleTitle: Large Deviations and Effective Equidistribution
abstract: We study large deviations for measurable averaging operators on state spaces of dynamical systems. We prove a relatively sharp large deviation result in terms of the norm gap of the averaging operator. Developing ideas of Linnik and Ellenberg, Michel, and Venkatesh, we deduce an effective equidistribution theorem. The novelty of our results is that they apply to measures with suboptimal bounds on the mass of Bowen balls. We present two new applications of our results. The first one is effective rigidity for the measure of maximal entropy on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D(2,1;\alpha )$</tex>-arithmetic quotients. This is a partial extension of a recent result of Rühr. The second one is non-escape of mass for measures having large entropy in a non-Archimedean place. This generalizes known results for real flows.

articleTitle: Sharp Estimates for Bubbling Solutions to Some Fourth-Order Geometric Equations
abstract: In this article, we derive an analogue of the exact bubbling rate formula of Chen–Lin [19] for the Q-curvature equation on closed four-dimensional Riemannian manifolds. Using this, we derive new existence results for the prescribed Q-curvature problem on closed four-dimensional Riemannian manifolds under a positive mass type assumption. Furthermore, as an other application, we deduce a compactness theorem for conformal metrics with prescribed Q-curvature on closed four-dimensional Riemannian manifolds under a nondegeneracy assumption. Our method is of variational nature and is based on the tools of critical points theory at infinity of Bahri [3]. Our exact bubbling rate formula is also used in a subsequent paper to interpret the index counting formula in [54] as the Leray–Schauder degree of the corresponding equation.

articleTitle: On the Genericity of Eisenstein Series and Their Residues for Covers of $GL_m$
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau_1^{(r)}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau_2^{(r)}$</tex> be two genuine cuspidal automorphic representations on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>-fold covers of the adelic points of the general linear groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_{n_1}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_{n_2}$</tex>, respectively, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E(g,s)$</tex> be the associated Eisenstein series on an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>-fold cover of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$GL_{n_1+n_2}$</tex>, normalized to have functional equation under <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s\mapsto 1-s$</tex>. Suppose <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Re(s)\geq 1/2$</tex> without loss. Then the value at any point of holomorphy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s=s_0$</tex> or the reside at any (simple) pole of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E(g,s)$</tex> is an automorphic form, and generates an automorphic representation. In this note we show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n_1\neq n_2$</tex> these automorphic representations (when not identically zero) are generic, while if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n_1=n_2:=n$</tex> they are generic except for residues at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s={n+1 \over 2n}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Superabundant Curves and the Artin Fan
abstract: We prove that every balanced one-dimensional polyhedral complex arises as the tropicalization of a smooth curve over a non-Archimedean field mapping to a toric Artin fan, namely the quotient of a toric variety by its dense torus.

articleTitle: Modular Representations of ${\rm GL}{(n)}$ Distinguished by ${\rm GL}{(n-1)}$ over a $p$-Adic Field
abstract: Abstract Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\it F}$</tex> be a non-Archimedean locally compact field, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex> be the cardinality of its residue field, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\it R}$</tex> be an algebraically closed field of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex> not dividing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>. We classify all irreducible smooth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\it R}$</tex>-representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}_n({\it F})$</tex> having a non-zero <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}_{n-1}({\it F})$</tex>-invariant linear form, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex> is not congruent to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> mod <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex>. Partial results in the case when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> mod <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex> show that, unlike the complex case, the space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}_{n-1}({\it F})$</tex>-invariant linear forms has dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2$</tex> for certain irreducible representations.

articleTitle: Symmetric invariants of ${\scr {g}}$-contractions and other semi-direct products
abstract: Abstract Suppose that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma $</tex> is a complex reductive Lie algebra. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\scr {g}}$</tex> be an involution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ}/2{\BBZ}$</tex>, which defines a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\scr {g}} = {\scr {g}}{_0} \oplus {\scr {g}}{_1}$</tex>-grading <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\scr {g}}{_0}: = {\scr {g}}{^\sigma }$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\scr {g}}$</tex> is a symmetric subalgebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBZ}{_2}$</tex>. The corresponding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\scr {g}}$</tex>-contraction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathop \limits^ {\scr {g}} = {\scr {g}}{_0}{\scr {g}}{_1}$</tex> is the Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\scr {g}}{_1}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal S}{(\mathop \limits^ ){\scr {g}}^{\scr {g}}^{\mathop \limits^ }}$</tex> is a commutative ideal. The goal of this article is to find out whether the algebra of symmetric invariants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm{rk}}\,{\scr {g}}$</tex> is a polynomial ring in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bar {\cal M}_g}$</tex> variables. To this end we develop a more general theory of symmetric invariants related to semi-direct products.

articleTitle: Top Fourier Coefficients for Cuspidal Representations of Symplectic Groups
abstract: In this paper, we prove a conjecture by Ginzburg et al. that for cuspidal automorphic representations of symplectic groups the top Fourier coefficients must be distinguished. That is, the partition associated with each of them consists of even parts only, and the stabilizer of the character defining the Fourier coefficient is anisotropic. This result is parallel to a local result by Moeglin. We expect a similar statement and proof for orthogonal groups.

articleTitle: Polynomial Realisations of Lie (Super)Algebras and Bessel Operators
abstract: We study realisations of Lie (super)algebras in Weyl (super)algebras and connections with minimal representations. The main result is the construction of small realisations of Lie superalgebras, which we apply for two distinct purposes. Firstly it naturally introduces, and generalises, the Bessel operators for Jordan algebras in the study of minimal representations of simple Lie groups. Secondly, we work out the theoretical realisation concretely for the exceptional Lie superalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\ell ^2}({\BBZ})$</tex>, giving a useful hands-on realisation.

articleTitle: Singular Curves and Quasi-hereditary Algebras
Slopes of Non-hyperelliptic Fibrations in Positive Characteristic
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f:S\rightarrow B$</tex> be a non-hyperelliptic semi-stable surface fibration in positive characteristic with genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\geq17$</tex>. We show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_f^2\geq4\chi_f$</tex>.

articleTitle: Conditional Expectations of Random Holomorphic Fields on Riemann Surfaces
abstract: Abstract We study two conditional expectations: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_n(z| p)$</tex> of the expected density of critical points of Gaussian random holomorphic sections <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s_n \in {H^0(M,L^n)}$</tex> of powers of a positive holomorphic line bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(L,h)$</tex> over Riemann surfaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M,\omega)$</tex> given that the random sections vanish at a point and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_n(z|q)$</tex> of the expected density of zeros given that the random sections have a fixed critical point. The critical points are points <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\nabla_{h^n} s_n=0$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\nabla_{h^n}$</tex> is the smooth Chern connection of the Hermitian metric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h^n$</tex>. The main result is that the rescaling conditional expectations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_n(p+ {u \over {\sqrt n}}|p)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_n(q+ {u \over {\sqrt n}}|q)$</tex> have universal limits <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_\infty(u|0)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_\infty(v|0)$</tex> as the power of the line bundle tends to infinity. We will see that the short-distance behaviors of these two conditional expectations are quite different: the behavior between critical points and the conditioning zero is neutral while there is a repulsion between zeros and the conditioning critical point. But the long-distance behaviors of these two rescaling densities are the same.

articleTitle: The Local Langlands Conjecture for the p-Adic Inner Form of Sp4
abstract: Abstract This paper proves the local Langlands conjecture for the non-quasi-split inner form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {Sp}_{1,1}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {Sp}_4$</tex> over a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-adic field of characteristic 0, by studying the restriction of representations from the non-quasi-split inner form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {GSp}_{1,1}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {GSp}_4$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {Sp}_{1,1}.$</tex> The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-packets for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {Sp}_{1,1}$</tex> are constructed based on the earlier work on the local Langlands correspondence for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {GSp}_{1,1}$</tex> by Gan and Tantono. To parameterize them in terms of so-called <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>-groups, we establish and utilize the local Langlands correspondence for groups which participate in the theta correspondence with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {Sp}_{1,1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {GSp}_{1,1}.$</tex> An interesting phenomenon arises when two distinct members in an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-packet of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {GSp}_{1,1}$</tex> are restricted to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm {Sp}_{1,1}.$</tex>

articleTitle: The Number of Surfaces of Fixed Genus in an Alternating Link Complement
abstract: Abstract Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> be a prime alternating link with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex> crossings. We show that for each fixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>, the number of genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> incompressible surfaces in the complement of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is bounded by an explicitly given polynomial in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. Previous bounds were exponential in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G{L_3}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Detecting Asymptotic Non-regular Values by Polar Curves
abstract: We locate the Malgrange non-regular values of a given polynomial function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f:{\BBC}^n \to {\BBC}$</tex> by using a series of affine polar curves. We moreover show that all non-trivial Malgrange non-regular values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> are indicated by a single “super-polar curve” which we introduce here, providing also an effective algorithm of detection.
